parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation or documented facility ban; anti-discrimination law, courts corrected documents, and high courts require vulnerability assessments in immigration detention. Urban queer spaces and official nondiscrimination policies reduce visitor exposure. But prison/detention placement is unresolved and reportedly unprepared, lower-court practice is inconsistent, and bias-crime law remains pending. Head-of-state and ministerial hostility, far-right campaigns, and survey reports of disproportionate trans harassment raise social risk and lower confidence in recourse. Rule of law partially protects trans people, especially in cities, but official hostility and custody gaps keep this below the safer band.
